titleEn: One on Each Hook—Up It Goes!

pages.text: "Finished playing!" Lolo dropped a bucket and tossed a rope into the yard. A basket and a dry net lay anywhere. Four wall hooks were empty, but Lolo did not look at them.
Going for water, Lolo tripped on the rope. "Ow!" A boot stepped on the basin, splashing water. There was nowhere clear to put a foot.
The favorite pebble was missing too: smooth and greenish. Lolo tipped the basket and searched the box, but it was nowhere. Lolo sniffled.
Dad the fisherman came into the yard with a net over his shoulder. "Lolo, what is wrong?" He glanced around the messy yard.
Dad pointed to the row of empty hooks on the wall. "Each hook has its own thing. Net hook, bucket hook, basket hook." Lolo leaned forward, bracing on both paws.
Dad hung the net on a hook. A handspan of space cleared underfoot. "One on each hook—up it goes!" he sang. Lolo picked up the bucket and sprang up.
Up went the bucket, then the coiled rope, then the basket. Riri pointed to empty hooks one by one. "Which hook is for this?" As hooks filled, the yard grew roomier. One on each hook—up it goes!
Finally, when Lolo lifted the net, green flashed underneath. "My pebble!" Lolo held it tightly in both hands. "Tidying finds lost things too!"
Lolo happily ran through the empty middle of the yard. "One, gather things after play! Two, one on each hook! Three, pebble in my pocket!" All four hooks were full.
Dad hugged Lolo and patted their back. "A roomy yard means no tripping, right?" Lolo placed those boots beside Dad's and said, "One on each hook—up it goes!"
